correctness.rationale: Uniform parking functions have feasible loads satisfying every prefix sum ≥prefix length, with multinomial weight n!/∏m_j!. Conditioning all bins except a<b and total T leaves only r=m_a constraints R≤r≤T and a weight proportional to binom(T,r): exact symmetric-binomial lower truncation, including T=0. Pairing r>s and swapped masses proves load pair inequality and stochastic dominance. For three car preferences, equal endpoints contribute m_a m_b(m_a-m_b) to peak-minus-valley; Pollak cyclic shift controls equality patterns and yields p+ +p-=2p0. The feasible profile (n−1,0,...,0,1) but impossible swap makes positivity ≥(n+1)^(−n+1). Independent complete preference word enumeration gives (peaks,valleys) (4,3),(33,27),(355,305) for n=3,4,5. Analytic proof handles all n; finite experiments do not.
residual_risks: Pollak cyclic-shift correspondence is classical and cited but not reproved here; no sharp asymptotic gap claimed.
